findings.statement: PMID:42473996: CA9 is preferentially enriched in ccRCC tumor cells with low normal-kidney expression; CA9-targeted PET offers proof-of-concept noninvasive discrimination of ccRCC, warranting prospective validation (single study, not validated clinically). High CA9 PET uptake associated with PBRM1 loss-of-function. PMID:35795483 reports CAIX mRNA increased in HIV-associated kidney cancer.

NDUFA4L2 is predictive of poor survival in ccRCC and supports proliferation/colony formation in cell lines (PMID:34970493); increases glycolysis (PMID:36722045); enhances lipid deposition and Ca9 expression in the TRACK early-ccRCC model; also a marker of low- and high-grade ccRCC in tissue and EVs (PMID:41656939).

PMID:36204178: MT1G downregulated in ccRCC vs normal tissue, proposed negative regulator of ferroptosis and poor-prognosis biomarker. PMID:38906969: high MT1G correlated with advanced stage and poorer prognosis; elevated MT1G promoted growth and metastasis in vitro/in vivo and inhibits CPT1B via H3K14 trimethylation, increasing lipid droplets. Note: tumour-vs-normal downregulation yet high expression is adverse within tumours.

SAP30 suppresses MT1G and the p53 pathway; SAP30 upregulated in ccRCC with poor prognosis; authors suggest SAP30 and MT1G as potential prognostic markers and therapeutic targets (PMID:40247376 and related chunks).

Chunks report MT1X as an oncogene indicating prognosis in ccRCC, an independent prognostic factor correlated with T/M stage and grade, with increased expression linked to worse prognosis (bioinformatic plus some experimental work).

PMID:37760940: ENO2 potential diagnostic biomarker and independent prognostic predictor in ccRCC, promoting progression via Warburg-effect glycolysis. PMID:39091581: ENO2 high in ccRCC cell lines; knockdown inhibits glycolysis and promotes ferroptosis. PMID:36313709: ENO2 related to OS. Enolase 2 also associated with TKI resistance (lenvatinib, cabozantinib) in cell lines.

PMID:40852386 reports ALDOB as a prognostic biomarker and potential immunotherapy target in ccRCC, linked to Treg/Th17/neutrophil infiltration; PMID:38655323 reports independent prognostic value in KIRC; PMID:37083815 pan-cancer low expression. Bioinformatic-heavy evidence.

PFKP upregulated in ccRCC (PMID:34321910, PMID:36901940); PMID:40341002 reports PFKP among glycolysis-related biomarkers with diagnostic and prognostic potential. PMID:34321910 notes low PFKP expression correlated with poor OS, which is direction-discordant with upregulation in tumour.
PLIN2 consistently upregulated in ccRCC (PMID:36901940), part of a diagnostic IHC panel validated on 128 samples (PMID:34482820) and related to prognosis via GEPIA (PMID:35314744).

PMID:41158242 (pan-cancer): ABAT underexpressed in KIRC and predicts poor prognosis in KIRC; PMID:41813748: ABAT overexpression suppresses tumour growth, mediates cGAS-STING and interacts with PRMT5 (context of that study not clear from sentence).

In ccRCC, ACY1 is only reported as downregulated (PMID:34002044, with MAGI2-AS3). Other relations concern colorectal cancer (oncogene, radiotherapy target in cetuximab-resistant CRC), so ccRCC therapeutic relevance is not supported.
PMID:34266404: CXCR4 and C3 overexpressed in ccRCC and associated with prognosis (database mining, single bioinformatic study).

Strong omics/tractability ranking (rank 2) but no literature relations; chunks describe CD74 expressed in both cancer cells and macrophages in ccRCC with a potential protumor function, with functional significance still unclear.

caveats: Top convergence genes (EGFR, FAS, PIGR, ERBB2, TNFRSF10B, ATP1A1, PDGFRA, KDR, EPAS1) have 0 literature relations in this corpus; literature is silent on them despite omics/Open Targets support. EGFR search returned no relevant EGFR sentences.

Clinically validated targets (HIF-2alpha inhibitor belzutifan; VEGFR TKIs/ICI combinations as standard of care) appear in chunks but only by alias (HIF-2alpha, VEGFR) and not as EPAS1/KDR symbols, so they are not cited as gene evidence.
Most literature-backed candidates (MT1G, MT1X, ENO2, ALDOB, PFKP, PLIN2, ABAT, COXFA4L2) rest on single or few bioinformatic/retrospective studies; none clinically validated as biomarker or target.

Contradictions: MT1G and PFKP are downregulated or upregulated in tumour vs normal yet high/low expression associated with adverse outcome in different studies; ACY1 evidence is mostly from colorectal cancer.
Corpus is ~320 abstracts; absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.
